title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Repaired pressure-compensated open-circuit hydraulic topology using the revised internally piloted forward sequence valve. Tank.S feeds Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P, ClampDCV.P, and ForwardSequenceValve.P. Relief and all valve returns/drains return directly to Tank.R. The forward drill supply is gated by the self-piloted ForwardSequenceValve supplied from Pump.P; when the clamp-apply pressure threshold is reached, ForwardSequenceValve.A supplies DrillDCV.P without relying on an external pilot from a load-locked clamp chamber. The clamp axis uses a float-centre ClampDCV and a dual pilot-operated check load lock at the clamp cylinder ports; during drill feed and drill retract the clamp DCV is neutral so A and B vent to tank and the load lock holds the already-applied clamp without a powered clamp-extend path. Drill feed uses exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-side meter-out exhaust path. Clamp release is gated by the externally piloted ReverseSequenceValve: ClampDCV.B supplies ReverseSequenceValve.P, while DrillDCV remains in retract and supplies ReverseSequenceValve.X from the drill retract pressure node; after drill retraction is pressure-confirmed, ReverseSequenceValve opens and supplies the clamp rod side through the load lock.

motion_control_decisions.phase_name: Clamp hold during drilling and drill return
motion_control_decisions.justification: The clamp must retain the workpiece during drilling and must not release until drill retraction is confirmed; static load retention is required, with no overrunning load.
Release speed is not specified and the horizontal load is not gravity-overrunning; no deliberate metering or dynamic load control is required by the statement.
Only a numeric feed speed is specified; no adjustable or load-independent feed control is stated. Horizontal drilling load is resistive.
Retract speed is not specified; horizontal axis is not gravity-overrunning and no holding requirement is stated for the drill axis.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power, relief, and return manifold
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and control branches; ReliefValve.T returns to Tank.R for pressure limiting.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp cylinder with directional valve and pilot-check load lock
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ClampDCV extend supplies the cap chamber through ClampLoadLock for apply. ClampDCV neutral vents pilot/work lines while ClampLoadLock holds during drilling and drill retraction. ClampDCV retract supplies the rod chamber through the reverse sequence gate for release.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Float-centre DCV paired with dual pilot-operated check load lock
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Dual pilot checks block actuator reverse flow when command pressure is removed; the float-centre DCV vents both work lines in neutral so the load-lock pilot pressures decay and the checks reseat.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Forward pressure sequence: clamp reaches pressure before drill feed
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve is supplied from Pump.P and opens by internal pressure operation when pressure reaches the clamp sequence threshold. Once open, ForwardSequenceValve.A supplies DrillDCV.P independent of ClampDCV.A, avoiding reliance on a load-locked or centred clamp work line.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Drill feed directional control with rod-side meter-out
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: During drill feed, DrillDCV extend supplies DrillCylinder.Cap while DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust flows through DrillFeedFlowControl A-to-B before returning through DrillDCV.B-T. Reverse B-to-A flow is internal to the one-way flow control for drill retract.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Reverse pressure sequence: drill retracts before clamp release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReverseSequenceValve blocks the clamp release work line from ClampDCV.B to ClampLoadLock.B1 until its X port senses drill retract pressure from DrillDCV.B. ForwardSequenceValve remains pump-pressure operated so the drill retract pressure node is maintained for the reverse interlock.

design_decisions.decision: Use a pressure-compensated variable pump with open-circuit tank and relief protection.
design_decisions.rationale: The repaired clamp holding state uses a float-centre ClampDCV with P blocked and A/B vented for load-lock pilot decay; a pressure-compensated variable pump provides standby flow reduction for this blocked-P neutral while the relief valve protects the system pressure line.

design_decisions.decision: Use a float-centre clamp DCV with a dual pilot-operated check load lock.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp must hold without relying on DCV leakage. Float-centre neutral vents both work lines to tank so pilot pressure can decay and the dual load lock can reseat, while P is blocked instead of unloading the drill supply.

design_decisions.decision: Use an internally piloted forward sequence valve supplied from Pump.P.
design_decisions.rationale: The external pilot from the clamp actuator-side load-locked chamber was removed because it is not pump-supplied when ClampDCV is neutral or retracting. The replacement sequence valve uses pressure at its own Pump.P-fed inlet, so drill supply remains available after the sequence threshold without depending on ClampDCV.A.

design_decisions.decision: Place ClampDCV in neutral during drill feed and drill retract.
design_decisions.rationale: During drilling and drill return the clamp axis is held hydraulically by ClampLoadLock, eliminating a powered clamp-extend path that would create forbidden active overlap with the drill-feed motion phase.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one one-way flow control in the drill rod-side exhaust path.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed drill feed phase requires non-compensated adjustable meter-out at the rod chamber; reverse flow through the one-way control permits drill retract without a second flow-control valve.

design_decisions.decision: Use a second externally piloted sequence valve as the reverse-order clamp-release interlock.
design_decisions.rationale: Forward pressure sequencing alone does not enforce drill-retract-before-clamp-release. The reverse sequence valve blocks clamp release flow until drill retract pressure is present at its X port while ClampDCV.B supplies its P port.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add clamp apply or clamp release flow-control valves.
design_decisions.rationale: Those phases are sizing_only; numeric speed targets are deferred to cylinder and pump sizing rather than extra throttling hardware.

evidence_gaps.reason: The supplied synthesis supports sequence valves generally but states that a direct cited complete schematic for this composed reverse-order interlock is not available.
evidence_gaps.evidence_needed: Engineering review or additional reference for the exact reverse-sequence clamp-release gate arrangement.

assumptions: Sequence valve cracking pressures, pump compensation setting, pump displacement, cylinder bore/rod dimensions, and line losses are deferred to sizing.
Clamp apply corresponds to ClampCylinder cap-end pressurization; clamp release corresponds to rod-end pressurization.
Drill feed corresponds to DrillCylinder cap-end pressurization; drill retract corresponds to rod-end pressurization.
ForwardSequenceValve is internally piloted from its Pump.P-fed inlet and has no external X port.
During drill feed and drill retract, ClampDCV is commanded neutral so the clamp is held by ClampLoadLock rather than by an active extend path.
During clamp_release, DrillDCV remains in retract until the reverse sequence valve is piloted open and clamp release is complete.
open_issues: Sizing must verify cylinder areas, pump flow, pressure losses, pump compensation setting, relief setting, and sequence settings against the stated force, speed, and maximum-pressure requirements.
Command timing/state chart must place ClampDCV in neutral during drill feed and drill retract so the clamp is held by ClampLoadLock, not by an active extend path.
During clamp_release, DrillDCV must remain in retract until the reverse sequence valve is piloted open and clamp release is complete.
Machine safety standards and risk assessment were not supplied and remain outside this topology selection.
The exact composed reverse pressure-piloted interlock should receive engineering review because the supplied synthesis does not include a direct cited complete schematic for that arrangement.

ForwardSequenceValve is internally piloted from the common Pump.P inlet rather than from a clamp-pressure node that proves the workpiece clamp has reached the required pressure condition. With ClampDCV neutral or with an early drill-feed command, Pump.P can deadhead and reach the sequence setting without clamp application, allowing DrillDCV.P to be supplied. This does not hydraulically enforce the required clamp-pressure-to-drill-feed transition.

research_coverage.summary: Most component classes and forward operating principles are supported by cited hydraulic training/technical sources: open-circuit pump/reservoir/relief topology, double-acting cylinders with directional valves, pilot-operated check load holding, meter-out drill feed speed control, and pressure-sequence-valve clamping-before-drilling without electrical sensing. The critical gap is the reverse/release interlock: the accumulated evidence supports that the drill/feed actuator can retract through a sequence-valve bypass, but it does not yet support a complete hydraulic topology that prevents clamp release until the drill feed axis has retracted. Because that is an explicit safety/sequence requirement, design cannot proceed safely and unambiguously.

items.rationale: Findings include cited guidance for an open hydraulic circuit: reservoir/tank feeds pump suction, pump outlet feeds pressure/control valves, returns go to tank, and a relief valve is connected in parallel with the pump/pressure line to discharge excess flow to tank. Evidence also distinguishes open-center low-pressure neutral from closed-center relief-limited neutral.

Findings support a double-acting clamp cylinder controlled by a directional valve, with work ports connected through pilot-operated check/load-holding valves. Cited sources support A/B-to-tank neutral for pilot-check reseating and warn not to rely on spool leakage for holding.

The required clamp phases are apply/extend, hold, and release/retract with no special speed regulation. Findings support powered extend/retract by a double-acting cylinder and directional valve, positive hold by pilot-operated check valves, and automatic transition from clamp completion/pressure rise to the next drilling/feed operation using a pressure sequence valve. The separate release-after-drill-retract interlock remains weak under the system sequence/load-holding needs, but the basic clamp actuator motion pattern is covered.

Cited sources support pilot-operated check valves or double pilot-operated check valves in cylinder work-port lines to prevent creep/lock the cylinder, with cross-piloting from the opposite commanded line and a neutral center that vents A/B pilot pressure to tank so checks close. This covers load-holding and controlled release at the actuator level.

Findings support a double-acting hydraulic feed cylinder with a directional valve for extend/retract. Neutral behavior is addressed by cited guidance: do not rely on blocked-center spool leakage for holding; use A/B-to-tank neutral with pilot-operated checks if positive holding is needed, and select valves compatible with meter-out backpressure.

Findings support meter-out feed control: restrict fluid leaving the cylinder for smooth hydraulic motion, use a one-way flow-control/needle valve with free reverse flow, and place it in the exhaust branch for extension so rod-end exhaust is throttled during drill feed while reverse/retract flow can bypass the restriction. The need does not require a cited drill-specific schematic identical to the requested machine.

Forward sequence is well supported: a normally closed pressure sequence valve in the drill/feed supply line can block the second actuator until clamp pressure rises above an adjustable setting, with external drain and reverse-flow bypass check. However, the accumulated evidence does not yet support the full multi-actuator interlock that clamp release is hydraulically prevented until the drill feed axis has retracted. Current reverse-flow evidence only says the later actuator can retract through a bypass check; it does not show or justify how clamp retraction is delayed/blocked until drill retraction is complete.

Leak-resistant clamp holding itself is covered by cited pilot-operated check valve guidance. The missing safety claim is the sequence-dependent holding requirement: the clamp must remain clamped during drilling and release must not be possible until the drill retracts. The findings do not yet provide cited connection logic for a hydraulic reverse-sequence or interlock valve arrangement that enforces that condition.

Findings support a no-electrical hydraulic pressure-threshold transition using a normally closed adjustable sequence valve. Cited sources state sequence valves open at an adjustable crack pressure after the first actuator completes motion and pressure builds, including clamping-before-drilling examples. This is sufficient to set the drill-feed enable threshold to the required approximate clamp pressure, subject to normal component selection/sizing.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing critical claim: a cited hydraulic connection pattern that prevents clamp release/retraction until the drill feed actuator has fully retracted, not merely a bypass that allows the drill actuator to retract.

Weak integration detail: existing sequence-valve evidence covers clamp-first/drill-second extension well, but reverse-stroke sequencing or a clamp-release interlock needs primary technical support before topology design proceeds.

design_issues.description: ForwardSequenceValve is internally piloted from the common Pump.P inlet rather than from a clamp-pressure node that proves the workpiece clamp has reached the required pressure condition. With ClampDCV neutral or with an early drill-feed command, Pump.P can deadhead and reach the sequence setting without clamp application, allowing DrillDCV.P to be supplied. This does not hydraulically enforce the required clamp-pressure-to-drill-feed transition.

The reverse pressure-piloted clamp-release interlock is a plausible composed sequence-valve pattern, and the topology implements the intended drill-retract pressure gate, but the supplied research still lacks a direct cited complete schematic for this exact reverse-order arrangement. This does not by itself prevent the requested behavior, but it should receive targeted engineering evidence or review.

design_review.summary: Invalid. The drill feed supply is gated by a sequence valve that senses common pump pressure, not verified clamp pressure, so the required hydraulic clamp-pressure interlock can be bypassed by pump deadheading or an early drill command. Other main elements—relief placement, clamp pilot-check holding with vented neutral, drill rod-side meter-out, and reverse pressure-sequence release gating—are topologically consistent, aside from the nonblocking evidence gap for the exact reverse interlock pattern.
